characters.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve / game sprite animation correction. Reference is our approved pixel survivor 01-gleb. Preserve EXACT hairstyle, glasses, outfit colours and character identity from the reference. Create ONE transparent sprite sheet with exactly EIGHT columns and TWO rows, each cell same size. Row 1: profile running WEST (facing left); Row 2: profile running EAST (facing right). Eight frames left to right form ONE COMPLETE TWO-STEP STRIDE, not eight variations of one step. Frame 0 near leg fully forward, far leg back; 1 near-leg weight acceptance, far leg lifts; 2 far knee passes forward; 3 near leg pushes off, far leg swings forward; frame 4 far leg fully forward and near leg back (opposite of frame 0); 5 far-leg weight acceptance, near leg lifts; 6 near knee passes forward; 7 far leg pushes off, near leg swings forward toward frame 0. Alternate BOTH feet visibly. The near trouser leg is slightly lighter and far leg darker so the reversal is unambiguous. Arms counter-swing with opposite leg. Constant body size, head and hips anchored to identical cell positions, minimal 1-pixel vertical bob, running IN PLACE without lateral drift. Crisp low-resolution pixel game character, body about 54 native pixels high, overhead game profile slightly elevated viewpoint, not realistic anatomy render, not smooth painting. No weapons, backpacks, scenery, text, labels, ground, shadows or grid lines. Each character fully inside its cell with generous transparent margin and all feet visible. Do not mirror a half-cycle to invent the second step: draw both leg phases. Equal grid, consistent head position in every frame.
